title: Arts, Sports & Inventions
subtitle: The Group of Seven, hockey heroes, Terry Fox and great Canadian discoveries

questions.question: The Group of Seven, founded in 1920, is famous for what?
options: A style of painting capturing the rugged wilderness landscapes
questions.explanation: In the visual arts Canada is perhaps best known for the Group of Seven, founded in 1920, who developed a style of painting to capture the rugged wilderness landscapes.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Arts and Culture in Canada (p. 25)

questions.question: Which artist painted the forests and Aboriginal artifacts of the West Coast?
questions.explanation: Emily Carr painted the forests and Aboriginal artifacts of the West Coast. Jean-Paul Riopelle was a pioneer of modern abstract art, and Kenojuak Ashevak pioneered modern Inuit art.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Arts and Culture in Canada (p. 25)

questions.question: Who pioneered modern Inuit art with etchings, prints and soapstone sculptures?
questions.explanation: Kenojuak Ashevak pioneered modern Inuit art with etchings, prints and soapstone sculptures.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Arts and Culture in Canada (p. 25)

questions.question: Which of these is a noteworthy Canadian filmmaker named in the guide?
questions.explanation: The films of Denys Arcand have been popular in Quebec and across the country and have won international awards. Other noteworthy Canadian filmmakers include Norman Jewison and Atom Egoyan.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Arts and Culture in Canada (p. 25)

questions.question: Who invented basketball, and in what year?
questions.explanation: Basketball was invented by Canadian James Naismith in 1891.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Modern Canada (p. 26)

questions.question: Who became a world record sprinter and double Olympic gold medallist at the 1996 Summer Games?
questions.explanation: In 1996 at the Olympic Summer Games, Donovan Bailey became a world record sprinter and double Olympic gold medallist.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Modern Canada (p. 26)

questions.question: What was Terry Fox's "Marathon of Hope"?
options: A wheelchair trip around the globe for spinal cord research
A cross-country run begun in 1980 to raise money for cancer research
questions.explanation: In 1980 Terry Fox, a British Columbian who lost his right leg to cancer at 18, began a cross-country run, the Marathon of Hope, to raise money for cancer research. He did not finish and later died of cancer, but yearly fundraising events continue in his name.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Modern Canada (p. 26)

questions.question: In 1985, which British Columbian circled the globe in a wheelchair to raise funds for spinal cord research?
questions.explanation: In 1985 Rick Hansen circled the globe in a wheelchair to raise funds for spinal cord research. Chantal Petitclerc became a world champion wheelchair racer and Paralympic gold medallist.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Modern Canada (p. 26)

questions.question: Wayne Gretzky, one of the greatest hockey players of all time, played for which team from 1979 to 1988?
questions.explanation: Wayne Gretzky played for the Edmonton Oilers from 1979 to 1988.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Modern Canada (p. 26)

questions.question: In 1972, who scored the winning goal for Canada in the Canada–Soviet Summit Series, "the goal heard around the world"?
questions.explanation: In 1972 Paul Henderson scored the winning goal in the Canada–Soviet Summit Series, remembered as an important event in both sports and cultural history.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Modern Canada (p. 26)

questions.question: What is the significance of the discovery of insulin by Sir Frederick Banting and Charles Best?
options: It is a hormone to treat diabetes that has saved 16 million lives worldwide
It allowed the first heart transplant
It led to the invention of the pacemaker
questions.explanation: Sir Frederick Banting of Toronto and Charles Best discovered insulin, a hormone to treat diabetes that has saved 16 million lives worldwide.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: Who invented the worldwide system of standard time zones?
questions.explanation: Sir Sandford Fleming invented the worldwide system of standard time zones.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: Who invented the snowmobile?
questions.explanation: Joseph-Armand Bombardier invented the snowmobile, a light-weight winter vehicle.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: Who invented the first cardiac pacemaker?
questions.explanation: Dr. John A. Hopps invented the first cardiac pacemaker, used today to save the lives of people with heart disorders. Dr. Wilder Penfield was a pioneering brain surgeon known as "the greatest living Canadian."
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: What is the Canadarm?
options: A prosthetic limb invented in Toronto
A robotic arm used in outer space, invented by SPAR Aerospace and the National Research Council
questions.explanation: SPAR Aerospace and the National Research Council invented the Canadarm, a robotic arm used in outer space. Since 1989 the Canadian Space Agency and Canadian astronauts have taken part in space exploration.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: Mike Lazaridis and Jim Balsillie of Research in Motion (RIM) are known for which invention?
questions.explanation: Mike Lazaridis and Jim Balsillie of Research in Motion, a wireless communications company, are known for its most famous invention: the BlackBerry.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: Who sent the first wireless voice message in the world, contributing to the invention of radio?
questions.explanation: Reginald Fessenden contributed to the invention of radio, sending the first wireless voice message in the world.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: True or false: Alexander Graham Bell hit on the idea of the telephone at his summer house in Canada.
questions.explanation: True. Alexander Graham Bell hit on the idea of the telephone at his summer house in Canada.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: True or false: Matthew Evans and Henry Woodward invented the first electric light bulb and later sold the patent to Thomas Edison.
questions.explanation: True. Evans and Woodward together invented the first electric light bulb and later sold the patent to Thomas Edison, who more famously commercialized it.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Great Canadian Discoveries and Inventions (p. 27)

questions.question: True or false: Mordecai Richler, Margaret Laurence and Stephen Leacock are among the Canadian writers named in the guide.
questions.explanation: True. The guide lists men and women of letters including Stephen Leacock, Louis Hémon, Sir Charles G.D. Roberts, Pauline Johnson, Émile Nelligan, Robertson Davies, Margaret Laurence and Mordecai Richler.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, Arts and Culture in Canada (p. 25)
